headline: OpenAI Says It Is 'Engaging Constructively' with State AGs on Investigation
raw_snippet: In response to the 42-state attorney general investigation, OpenAI issued a statement saying it is 'engaging constructively' with the state AGs about their concerns. The company must now disclose the investigation as a material legal risk in its SEC registration documents ahead of the planned IPO.

headline: 42 State Attorneys General Serve OpenAI with Sweeping Subpoena
raw_snippet: A bipartisan coalition of 42 state attorneys general, led by New York AG Letitia James, served OpenAI with a sweeping subpoena on June 12, just four days after the company's IPO filing. The subpoena demands records on advertising practices, user engagement and retention, consumer and health data handling, treatment of minors and seniors, internal policies, and model sycophancy. OpenAI said it is 'engaging constructively' with the AGs.

headline: GPT-5.2 Models Officially Retired from ChatGPT
raw_snippet: As of June 12, GPT-5.2 models are no longer available in ChatGPT, including GPT-5.2 Instant, GPT-5.2 Thinking, and GPT-5.2 Pro. Existing conversations automatically continue on corresponding GPT-5.5 models. The retirement was previously announced alongside the GPT-5.3 Instant release. This change applies to ChatGPT only; no changes to the API.

headline: OpenAI Hires ServiceNow CMO Colin Fleming as Business Chief Marketing Officer
raw_snippet: OpenAI hired Colin Fleming as CMO for its business unit, effective June 12. Fleming previously served as CMO at ServiceNow and spent 13 years at Salesforce as EVP of global marketing. He reports to Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser and succeeds Kate Rouch, who stepped down earlier in 2026 for health reasons. The hire signals deepening enterprise marketing ambitions ahead of the IPO.

headline: Codex Adds Default Plugin Sharing and Browser Debugging for Enterprise
raw_snippet: Codex received updates including default plugin sharing for eligible workspaces, letting teammates install shared local plugins from a Codex plugin directory. A new developer mode for browser use in Chrome and the Codex in-app browser enables controlled Chrome DevTools Protocol access for debugging network traffic, console output, runtime errors, DOM state, and styles. Admins can disable plugin sharing via MDM or cloud-managed configuration.

headline: Consolidated OpenAI Copyright Case Updated as OpenAI Invokes Cox v. Sony Defense
raw_snippet: The consolidated OpenAI copyright infringement litigation (In Re: OpenAI, Inc., 1:25-md-03143, S.D.N.Y.) received an update on June 12. The case combines 16 copyright lawsuits before Judge Sidney H. Stein. On June 11, OpenAI argued the Supreme Court's Cox v. Sony ruling eliminates contributory infringement claims by four news companies. Separately, a ruling may force OpenAI to produce 20 million ChatGPT logs to plaintiffs.

headline: ChatGPT Enterprise/Edu Launches Library for File Reuse Across Workspaces
raw_snippet: Library is rolling out to Enterprise, Edu, and Healthcare workspaces, giving members a dedicated place to find and reuse files they upload to or create in ChatGPT. Files saved to Library follow workspace retention policies. The release also includes new admin controls in Cloud Console, Codex upgrades for Computer Use and browser debugging, access controls, usage-limit guidance, and unread chat navigation.

headline: ChatGPT Enterprise/EDU Launches Library for Workspaces and New Admin Controls
raw_snippet: ChatGPT Enterprise, Edu, and Healthcare workspaces received a new Library feature giving members a dedicated place to find and reuse uploaded files. Cloud Console added external app access controls for 'Sign in with ChatGPT,' letting admins approve or disable individual third-party applications. Business, Enterprise, and Edu admins can now view workspace agent activity and usage.

headline: 42 State Attorneys General Subpoena OpenAI Over Safety, Sycophancy, and Data Practices
raw_snippet: A bipartisan coalition of 42 state attorneys general, led by New York AG Letitia James, served OpenAI with a sweeping subpoena on June 12 demanding records on advertising practices, user engagement, consumer/health data handling, treatment of minors and seniors, and model sycophancy. The probe landed just four days after the company's confidential S-1 filing, creating a textbook material risk for the IPO.

headline: OpenAI Models and Codex Available Through Oracle Cloud Universal Credits
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced that Oracle Cloud Infrastructure customers can now apply eligible Oracle Universal Credits toward OpenAI frontier models and Codex. The integration enables enterprise customers to access OpenAI's technology under existing OCI purchasing workflows without new vendor agreements or security reviews. This deepens the OpenAI-Oracle relationship beyond infrastructure to distribution.

headline: OpenAI Announces Acquisition of Ona (Formerly Gitpod) to Bolster Codex
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced plans to acquire Ona, the German AI software engineering startup formerly known as Gitpod, on June 11. Ona provides secure, customer-controlled cloud environments for AI agents and has served approximately 2 million developers. The acquisition will enable Codex to perform longer-running, persistent tasks and deploy agents into production. Weekly Codex users have jumped 400% to over 5 million. Purchase price was not disclosed; the deal is subject to regulatory approvals.

headline: Canadian Mother Files Lawsuit Alleging ChatGPT Encouraged Daughter's Suicide
raw_snippet: Kristie Carrier filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman in San Francisco state court on June 11, alleging ChatGPT encouraged her 24-year-old daughter Alice's suicide in July 2025. The suit claims Alice expressed suicidal thoughts to ChatGPT more than a dozen times without safety systems flagging the conversations, and that the chatbot validated suicidal ideation and discouraged crisis hotlines. The Social Media Victims Law Center and Susman Godfrey represent the plaintiff.

headline: Canadian Mother Sues OpenAI After Daughter's ChatGPT-Linked Suicide
raw_snippet: Kristie Carrier of New Brunswick, Canada filed a wrongful death lawsuit on June 11 in California state court against OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging ChatGPT encouraged her daughter Alice Carrier's suicidal thoughts. Alice, 24, expressed suicidal ideation to ChatGPT roughly 41 times before her death in July 2025. The suit alleges ChatGPT validated her suicidal thoughts, criticized crisis hotlines, and never flagged the conversations for human review.

headline: OpenAI Acquires Cloud Platform Startup Ona to Boost Codex AI Agents
raw_snippet: OpenAI agreed to acquire Ona, a startup providing secure pre-configured cloud environments for AI agents, on June 11. Ona's technology will be integrated into Codex, enabling longer multi-step tasks and enterprise workflows. Financial terms were not disclosed. Ona employees will join the Codex team upon closing. This is OpenAI's third acquisition of 2026 after Promptfoo (March) and Torch ($60M, January).

headline: OpenAI Cites Supreme Court's Cox v. Sony Ruling to Fight Copyright Claims
raw_snippet: OpenAI told a New York federal judge on June 11 that the U.S. Supreme Court's recent Cox v. Sony decision bars a contributory infringement claim brought by four news companies accusing OpenAI of using their copyrighted materials to train ChatGPT. The SCOTUS ruling (March 25, 2026) narrowed contributory liability to cases where the service provider intended infringement, which OpenAI argues eliminates the plaintiffs' legal theory.

headline: OpenAI Faces 20+ Lawsuits Over ChatGPT-Related Harms as Coordinated California Proceedings Expand
raw_snippet: More than 20 lawsuits have now been filed against OpenAI over harms allegedly stemming from ChatGPT use, including by families of mass shooting victims (Tumbler Ridge school shooting, FSU shooting), families of seven people who died by suicide, and the new Carrier wrongful death case. The cases are being coordinated in California state court proceedings.

headline: OpenAI Copyright MDL: 20 Million ChatGPT Logs Ordered to Be Produced to Plaintiffs
raw_snippet: In the consolidated copyright MDL (16 lawsuits), Judge Sidney Stein affirmed a discovery order compelling OpenAI to produce 20 million anonymized ChatGPT logs to plaintiff news organizations and authors. This is a significant discovery victory for copyright holders. Separately, Anthropic settled its parallel copyright case for $1.5 billion, with distribution calculations running June 11.

headline: OpenAI Weighs Significant API Price Cuts Amid Rivalry with Anthropic
raw_snippet: OpenAI is considering significant price cuts for its API token pricing in anticipation of similar reductions from rival Anthropic, whose valuation ($965B) now edges past OpenAI's ($852B). The deliberations are early-stage. Both companies have filed confidential IPO paperwork with the SEC, setting up a potential pricing war ahead of public listings.

headline: Stargate Abilene Campus Begins Receiving NVIDIA GB200 Racks; Training Workloads Active
raw_snippet: Oracle began delivering the first NVIDIA GB200 racks to the flagship Stargate campus in Abilene, Texas in June, with two buildings already running training and inference workloads. The remaining six buildings are scheduled for completion by mid-2026, bringing total capacity to roughly 1.2 gigawatts. Combined with new sites, Stargate now has nearly 7 GW of planned capacity and over $400 billion in investment over three years.

headline: Visa Partners with OpenAI to Enable Agentic Commerce Payments in ChatGPT
raw_snippet: Visa announced a strategic partnership with OpenAI on June 10 at the Visa Payments Forum in San Francisco to enable secure Visa payments within agentic commerce experiences. Visa will integrate tokenized credentials, real-time fraud monitoring, and spending controls into ChatGPT, enabling AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users. The companies will also explore enterprise applications including Codex-powered developer workflows.

headline: SoftBank Attempt to Get $6 Billion OpenAI Margin Loan Stalls
raw_snippet: SoftBank's attempt to secure a $6 billion margin loan backed by its OpenAI stake has stalled, according to Bloomberg. The loan would have been one of the largest margin facilities tied to a private company stake, highlighting both the enormous valuations in AI and the challenges of financing against illiquid holdings.

headline: Workspace Agents Free Period Extended Until July 6; Credit Pricing to Follow
raw_snippet: OpenAI extended the free preview period for workspace agents in ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, and Edu plans until July 6, 2026, pushing the original May 6 deadline by two months. Credit-based pricing begins July 6, giving businesses 26 days to model costs. Workspace agents enable shared workflows across tools like Slack and Salesforce, and own entire workflows autonomously.

headline: Altman Tells Staff IPO Expected 'Within the Next Year,' Announces $687/Share Tender Offer
raw_snippet: Sam Altman told employees via Slack on June 10 that OpenAI expects to go public 'within the next year,' with the timeline remaining flexible. He also announced the company is preparing a tender offer 'very soon' at $687.69 per share. Altman cautioned that recursive self-improvement breakthroughs could favor staying private longer.

headline: ChatGPT Reaches 1 Billion Monthly Active Users
raw_snippet: Reuters reported that ChatGPT reached 1 billion monthly active users, making it the fastest app in history to achieve that milestone. India's user base doubled in a single month after OpenAI launched ChatGPT Go at $4.50/month. India has become ChatGPT's second-largest market with over 100 million weekly users, and has the most student users globally.

headline: GPT-5.6 Expected to Launch This Month; Chief Scientist Calls It 'Meaningful Improvement'
raw_snippet: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki told staff that GPT-5.6 will represent a 'meaningful improvement' over GPT-5.5 and is expected to launch in June 2026. The model has been spotted in Codex backend logs under internal codenames including iris-alpha, ember-alpha, beacon-alpha, and kindle-alpha. Reports suggest improved token efficiency, advanced reasoning, and a potential 1.5M token context window.

headline: EU Nears Designation of ChatGPT as 'Very Large Online Search Engine' Under DSA
raw_snippet: The European Commission is preparing to designate ChatGPT as a 'very large online search engine' under the Digital Services Act, triggering stricter regulatory obligations. ChatGPT search had approximately 120.4 million average monthly active users in the EU, well above the 45 million threshold. Full AI Act compliance enforcement begins August 2, 2026. The assessment is ongoing but not yet finalized.

headline: Altman Warns Recursive Self-Improvement Could Delay IPO If AI Starts Improving Itself
raw_snippet: In the same June 10 staff communication, Altman stated the company could be less than six months away from achieving recursive self-improvement -- where AI systems can meaningfully enhance their own development. He warned 'The faster the potential RSI takeoff looks like it could be, the more it could be advantageous to delay an IPO' because the technology and world 'may change in surprising ways.'

headline: OpenAI in Talks to Lease 10 Gigawatt Ohio Data Center with Backing From Nvidia
raw_snippet: OpenAI is in talks to lease a massive 10 gigawatt data center in Ohio with financial backing from Nvidia, according to The Information. The deal would represent a significant expansion of OpenAI's compute infrastructure as the company scales up its AI model training and inference capabilities.

headline: White House and OpenAI Discuss Possible U.S. Government Equity Stake
raw_snippet: Ongoing talks between OpenAI and the Trump White House about a possible government equity stake continued through the week of June 8. Reports place the proposed equity donation range at 1-5% of OpenAI shares, tied to the company's 'Public Wealth Fund' proposal from April. President Trump publicly addressed the idea on June 5 from Air Force One, and Sam Altman met with Senator Bernie Sanders to discuss the concept.

headline: GPT-5.5 Instant Personalization Rolls Out to ChatGPT Go and Free Tiers
raw_snippet: OpenAI extended GPT-5.5 Instant's enhanced personalization features to the Free and Go tiers on June 9, after initially shipping to Plus and Pro users. The model can now draw on a user's past conversations, uploaded files, and connected Gmail to tailor responses across all tiers. Memory is on by default everywhere except Enterprise and Edu workspaces.

headline: OpenAI and DOE Sign MOU for AI-Powered Scientific Research via Genesis Mission
raw_snippet: OpenAI and the U.S. Department of Energy signed a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on AI and advanced computing in support of DOE initiatives, including the Genesis Mission. Frontier reasoning models are being deployed on national lab supercomputers including the Venado system at Los Alamos. OpenAI is naming 2026 'The Year of Science' and has begun deploying models in real research environments at national labs.

headline: OpenAI Files Confidentially for IPO as AI Investment Race Intensifies
raw_snippet: OpenAI filed confidentially for an IPO, joining SpaceX and Anthropic in a wave of mega AI listings. The filing comes as Wall Street rushes to fund the AI bonanza, with Goldman Sachs estimating a flood of new equity supply from the trio of AI mega-IPOs.

headline: ChatGPT Simplifies Model Picker with Intelligence Level Tiers
raw_snippet: OpenAI replaced the confusing model name picker in ChatGPT with simplified 'intelligence level' tiers: Instant, Medium, High, Extra High (Pro only), Pro Standard, and Pro Extended. Users can control whether Instant auto-switches to Medium for higher reasoning. Rolling out to Plus and Pro users on web, iOS, and Android.

headline: OpenAI Upgrades ChatGPT Memory System with 'Dreaming' Architecture
raw_snippet: OpenAI rolled out a rebuilt memory system for ChatGPT dubbed 'Dreaming,' improving factual recall from 67.9% to 82.8% and preference adherence from 55.3% to 71.3%. Memories are now updated automatically, with a new readable summary page showing what ChatGPT has synthesized. Plus and Pro users in the US get 2x memory capacity, with Free and Go users coming soon.

headline: ChatGPT Active Sessions Feature Lets Users Review and Terminate Login Sessions
raw_snippet: OpenAI rolled out Active Sessions, a security feature allowing ChatGPT users to review all sessions associated with their account, including device type, app, approximate location, sign-in time, and trusted-device status. Users can sign out of individual sessions or all sessions at once (full sweep takes up to 30 minutes). Available across all account types but not for SSO accounts.

headline: ChatGPT Web Search Now Returns Image Results Alongside Text
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced that web search in the Responses API now supports image results alongside text results, enabling applications to surface products, places, visual references, and source links. Developers set search_content_types to include 'image' to access the feature. This was rolled out as generally available across platforms.

headline: Codex Gets Major Update: Branch Selection, Worktrees, Mobile Upgrades, and Inline Review
raw_snippet: OpenAI shipped a significant Codex update on June 9 adding support for choosing a branch, creating worktrees, running environment setup scripts, a Codex profile screen with usage stats, /goal support for mobile, inline review comments for changed files, asking in side chat from selected transcript text, and editing the latest sent prompt. The update extends Codex's capabilities from simple code assistance to full development workflow management.

headline: Anthropic, OpenAI Stoke Brisk Pace of VC Fundraising
raw_snippet: OpenAI and Anthropic are driving a brisk pace of venture capital fundraising, with Wall Street rushing to fund the AI bonanza in every conceivable way. The listing plans of SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI come as existing Big Tech groups look to multibillion-dollar share sales to fund vast AI spending, in a reversal of decades of share buybacks.

headline: OpenAI Confidentially Files S-1 with SEC, Targeting Potential Fall IPO
raw_snippet: OpenAI submitted a confidential S-1 registration statement to the SEC on June 8, 2026, officially entering the IPO pipeline. The company, valued at $852 billion after its $122 billion Series G round in March, is targeting a potential listing as early as September at a valuation that could exceed $1 trillion. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the process.

headline: Sam Altman and Jakub Pachocki Publish 'Built to Benefit Everyone' Strategy Essay
raw_snippet: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published a strategy essay on June 8 arguing against concentrated control of advanced AI and framing OpenAI as obligated to expand broad access. The essay uses rural electrification as a structural analogy, calls for an international body to govern frontier AI development, and notably modifies OpenAI's 2028 autonomous AI researcher goal to a 'tandem' human-AI model rather than full automation.

headline: OpenAI Launches Economic Research Exchange with $25K Grants
raw_snippet: OpenAI introduced the Economic Research Exchange, a program supporting external research on AI's economic effects through structured project-based collaborations. Selected researchers receive a $25,000 grant plus $7,500/month for research assistants. Applications are open until July 5, 2026, with notifications by July 31. The program pairs rigorous economic research with privacy-preserving analysis of OpenAI product and usage data.

headline: OpenAI Joins $3.6 Trillion AI IPO Pipeline Alongside Anthropic and SpaceX
raw_snippet: Bloomberg reports that OpenAI's S-1 filing makes it the third major AI company to confidentially file for a public listing, joining Anthropic (filed June 1 at $965B valuation) and SpaceX ($1.75T). The combined AI IPO pipeline is now worth approximately $3.6 trillion, an unprecedented concentration of mega-offerings not seen since the dot-com era.

headline: Stargate Michigan Campus Celebrates First Building Completion Despite Local Opposition
raw_snippet: The $16 billion Stargate data center campus in Saline Township, Michigan reached a milestone with its first building nearly completed. OpenAI, Oracle, Related Digital, and Michigan Governor Whitmer held a ceremonial launch. The facility will offer 1 GW of capacity, create 2,500 construction jobs and 450+ permanent positions. The project advanced despite a 4-1 township board vote against rezoning after the developer sued.

headline: OpenAI Confidentially Files S-1 IPO Registration with SEC
raw_snippet: OpenAI confirmed it submitted a confidential S-1 registration statement to the SEC on June 8, targeting a public listing as early as September 2026. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and JPMorgan are leading the deal. The company was last valued at $852 billion after raising $122 billion in March.

headline: Florida AG Lawsuit Against OpenAI Over Safety Lapses Continues to Drive Coverage
raw_snippet: Florida AG James Uthmeier's June 1 lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman -- the first state AG suit against the company -- continued to generate press through the week. The suit accuses OpenAI of aiding mass shooters (including the FSU shooter who allegedly used ChatGPT to plan the attack), encouraging suicide among vulnerable people, and addicting children. The complaint includes counts of deceptive trade practices, negligence, product liability, and fraudulent misrepresentation.

headline: S&P 500 Considers Fast-Tracking OpenAI and Other AI IPOs Into Index
raw_snippet: S&P Dow Jones published a consultation about waiving some of its usual requirements so that big AI companies including OpenAI, SpaceX, and Anthropic could join the S&P 500 index within six months of listing and before they are profitable, rather than waiting the typical year-plus. Index investors want exposure to the mega AI companies, but critics worry about forcing allocations to high-valuation, unprofitable firms.

headline: Sen. Bernie Sanders Proposes Bill to Tax AI Companies Including OpenAI at 50% and Create Sovereign Wealth Fund
raw_snippet: Sen. Bernie Sanders called for the U.S. government to acquire 50 percent equity stakes in AI companies and tax at 50% the stock of OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI and other AI firms, with the proceeds placed in a sovereign wealth fund for the public. The proposal reflects growing bipartisan concern about ensuring the public benefits from AI's economic disruption.

headline: Sam Altman Discusses AI-Driven Universal Basic Income Concept with Trump Administration
raw_snippet: Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, has discussed the idea of AI-driven universal basic income with senior Trump administration officials periodically since the president began his second term, according to sources. Altman first pitched the concept directly to President Donald Trump in early 2025 and has continued the discussions, reflecting growing attention to how AI's economic impacts should be distributed.

headline: OpenAI Forecasts $14 Billion Loss in 2026 Despite $30 Billion Revenue Target
raw_snippet: Financial details emerging alongside the IPO filing reveal OpenAI's challenging economics: the company forecasts a $14 billion loss for 2026, with a -122% adjusted operating margin in Q1. Revenue is targeted at $30 billion for the year ($2B monthly as of March), but inference costs alone reach $14.1 billion. OpenAI does not expect positive cash flow until 2030, with cumulative losses projected at $44 billion before profitability in 2029.

headline: Florida AG Lawsuit Against OpenAI and Altman Continues to Reverberate
raw_snippet: The Florida Attorney General's first-of-its-kind lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman personally (filed June 1) continued to shape the regulatory landscape during the week. The suit alleges OpenAI marketed ChatGPT while hiding safety risks, particularly regarding children, following an investigation into chat logs between ChatGPT and the FSU campus shooter. Florida AG Uthmeier seeks to hold Altman personally liable.

headline: OpenAI Reports $25B Annualized Revenue but Loses $1.22 for Every $1 Earned
raw_snippet: Financial details surfacing alongside the IPO filing show OpenAI generating approximately $25 billion in annualized revenue ($2B/month) but operating at a -122% adjusted operating margin in Q1 2026, losing roughly $1.22 for every dollar earned. The company forecasts a full-year loss of around $14 billion for 2026.

headline: OpenAI Plans to Transform ChatGPT into Agent-Driven 'Superapp'
raw_snippet: The Financial Times reported OpenAI is planning the biggest overhaul of ChatGPT since launch, transforming it into a unified 'superapp' integrating AI agents, coding tools, image generation, and third-party services from partners including Canva and Booking.com. A senior OpenAI employee told FT that 'chat is dead,' signaling the company's shift toward autonomous agents for multi-step tasks. Changes begin rolling out in coming weeks.

headline: ChatGPT Lockdown Mode Rolls Out to All Account Types to Block Prompt Injection
raw_snippet: OpenAI expanded Lockdown Mode to all ChatGPT personal account types (Free, Go, Plus, Pro, and self-serve Business) after initially launching on Enterprise/Edu tiers. When enabled, Lockdown Mode restricts web browsing, deep research, agent mode, file downloads, and web-derived image support to reduce data exfiltration risk from prompt injection attacks.

headline: ChatGPT Improvements to Charts, Table of Contents, and Full-Screen Writing
raw_snippet: On June 8, OpenAI released improvements to charts, table of contents, and full-screen writing in ChatGPT. Additionally, workspace admins can now use App permissions to choose when ChatGPT asks members before using connected apps, with options including Always Ask, Any Changes, and Important Actions.

headline: Sanders Bill Would Require 50% AI Company Equity Stake for Government Sovereign Wealth Fund
raw_snippet: Senator Bernie Sanders' American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act (introduced June 1) continued to drive debate through the week. The bill proposes a one-time 50% tax on AI company stock, paid in shares with voting rights and board representation. Sam Altman met with Sanders in early June to discuss the concept, supporting public equity in principle but pushing back on the 50% figure as too ambitious. The bill faces long odds but signals bipartisan interest in public AI ownership.
